newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian High Court upholds excise challenge.
newsitem.headline: Australian High Court upholds excise challenge.

text.p: Australia's High Court on Tuesday upheld a challenge against the right of states and territories to levy excises, casting doubt on billions of dollars of state revenue.
In a four to three majority judgement, the court ruled that tobacco franchise fees levied by the state of New South Wales were in fact a tax.
Australia's constitution bans states and territories from levying a tax, giving the national government sole power to impose excises and customs duties.
Media reports on Tuesday said the national government had a A$5 billion emergency tax package drafted to replace a string of state charges if the court upheld the challenge.
"We are conscious that this judgement has the most serious implications for the revenues of the states and territories," the majority judgement said.
Tuesday's ruling effectively outlaws state and territory business franchise fees on tobacco, alcohol and petrol which account for about 16 percent of state and territory revenue.
New South Wales and other states had argued that the franchise fee, based on sales, was a licence fee for the right to sell tobacco and other goods.
But the High Court's majority judgement ruled it was clearly a tax and therefore invalid under the constitution.
